blocks.text: Key facts about Consuelo Giant Duhat

blocks.caption: Key facts of Consuelo Giant Duhat

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Consuelo Giant Duhat was about 27 years old and about 5.5 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 60 to 70 kg / season. It bears fruit in April May. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

A fruit of Consuelo Giant Duhat weighs about 18.2 grams, and its shape is oblong to ellipsoid. The flesh is purplish white and smooth and firm. Its sweetness measured 14.7 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 82.3 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is April May, bearing annual to regular.
Where and when to plant Consuelo Giant Duhat

Pick a variety by the fruit your buyers pay for: its size, sweetness and flesh, and how regularly the tree bears. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).
